name: Abū al-Ṭayyib Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī al-Mutanabbī
summary: The great poet of the fourth/tenth century, born in Kufa in 303/915, panegyrist of Sayf al-Dawla in Aleppo; Ibn al-Anbārī gives him a long entry for his learning in the language, and his verses were a field of the grammarians.
bio: Al-Mutanabbī was born in Kufa in 303/915, grew up in Syria and lived among the Bedouin, seeking letters and the science of Arabic, and took up poetry in his youth until he surpassed the poets of his age. He praised the Ḥamdānid Sayf al-Dawla in Aleppo, then went to Egypt to Kāfūr, and later to Persia.

He was killed on his way back to Iraq in 354/965. Ibn al-Anbārī's long entry gathers his exchanges with the grammarians of his day: his verse was commented on and disputed by Ibn Jinnī, al-Wāḥidī and others.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 366–374
